_comment: Symbol-size ratchet pins (#1155). MEASURED values, never round ceilings. Taken at the bench's own flags (Release = -O3 -DNDEBUG -std=c++23) on the toolchain named below; sizes are compiler-bound, so the gate refuses to compare across toolchains. Re-pin with: python3 bench/symbol_ratchet.py --build bench/build --pins bench/symbol_ratchet.json --emit

symbols.note: RE-PINNED 1474 -> 1613 (+139) by #894 (ADR-0080 reclaim_local). The ONLY pinned symbol this change moves — the other four are byte-identical — and the growth is fully attributed at instruction level: ONE `addl $1,%fs:` on entry, plus a 5-instruction exit epilogue emitted THREE times (the wide TLS-buffer path, the small/stack path, and the .cold unwind clone), plus `nop` re-padding and two cleanup-frame displacement changes that add no instruction. The per-edge dispatch loop body is byte-identical, so the cost is once per fan_out regardless of subscriber count, and the no-subscriber early return is untouched. Priced on the bench: `inproc-batch` fanout-1 (the batch-calibrated bare-notify case) 102 ns -> 102 ns p50, +0.00%, against a same-day A/A null of +/-0.8%. rv32 (-Os, GCC 15.2) is +24 B and +6 instructions on entry; `reclaim_strict` is +0 instructions here.

RE-PINNED 2023 -> 2231 (+208) by #1325 car 4 (RFC-0027 forwarder). The growth is ONE pass-through `std::span` — §6.1's minted reply-leg spelling — threaded into the three `[[gnu::flatten]]` `rebuild_fwd_forward` instantiations this hop inlines. Two cheaper shapes were measured and rejected: deciding the mint inside this hop cost +688 B, and a lazy supplier closure still cost +512 B; hoisting the decision to `route_fwd_ingress` (unpinned, and already switching on `kind`) leaves only the forwarded span. No new work executes on the request path: the `if (!is_reply)` branch that guarded the mount-run assignment became an `is_reply ? ... : ...` select on the same field. NOT priced on the bench yet — RFC-0027 §12.4 (car 5) is the gate that must, including the mandatory four-link reply-spread arm.
